proposals.title: Monorepo scaffold, toolchain, and ADR-009
proposals.why_now: The repository is empty. Every subsequent task depends on the directory structure, strict TypeScript configuration, blocking lint rules, and ADR-009 being written. The spec explicitly requires ADR-009 to exist before any state hash is implemented, and the determinism and dependency-boundary lints must be active before any package code is written — otherwise early code can silently violate ADR-002, ADR-003, or INV-26 in ways that are expensive to unwind.

CanonicalEncoder implementing ADR-009 spec: produces identical bytes for logically identical states, different bytes for different states, bigint distinct from safe integer in encoding
Intermediate multiplication for notional (Quantity * Price) performed entirely in bigint
Property test: no safe-integer overflow across a simulated ten-year replay sequence of counter increments (INV-23)

proposals.title: packages/core — branded types, positional RNG, CanonicalEncoder, arithmetic
proposals.why_now: Every other package imports core. The branded numeric types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick) are the enforcement mechanism for ADR-003 and ADR-004 — without them the domain and world packages cannot be written in spec-compliant TypeScript. The CanonicalEncoder must be implemented immediately after ADR-009 is written, before any state hash exists. The positional rand() function is the root of all determinism in the project.

proposals.title: packages/world — price generator with two noise layers and two assets
proposals.why_now: The price generator is required for FASE-1 and is a prerequisite for the canonical tick loop. It is the most algorithmically complex piece of FASE-1, and INV-02 (direct tick query equals tick-by-tick advance) is the most important test in the project per the spec. Starting it immediately after core allows maximum time for correctness validation. Getting the O(1) positionality wrong here invalidates determinism guarantees retroactively.

proposals.title: packages/domain — double-entry ledger and spot market order
proposals.why_now: The ledger and order execution layer is the other major FASE-1 prerequisite alongside the price generator. INV-04 through INV-07 (transaction balance, zero-sum BRL, zero-sum per asset, rounding residue) must be green for FASE-1 acceptance. These invariants are best established now while the ledger is small, before the complexity of the full tick loop and derivatives are added.

proposals.title: Canonical tick loop, save format, tools/replay, tools/bench, and minimum Electron shell
proposals.why_now: This completes FASE-1. The canonical tick processing order (Section 7) must be implemented in a single legible location with a test verifying the order. The save format (ADR-006) plus tools/replay enables INV-01. tools/bench with frozen calibration ratios establishes the performance baseline. The minimum Electron installer is a FASE-1 hard requirement — the spec states explicitly that the installer must exist in FASE-1 even if the application does little, because deferred packaging has caused unrecoverable architecture failures in practice.

repository_assessment.current_state: Repository is empty: no packages, no apps, no tools, no ADRs, no source files. Only the frozen specification, benchmark infrastructure directories, and a README exist. Zero acceptance criteria for any phase have been met.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: No repository scaffold exists. The monorepo structure, TypeScript strict toolchain, blocking lint rules, and ADR-009 (CanonicalEncoder specification) must all be established before any implementation code can be written in spec compliance.

warnings: Hash function is a DEFINIR item: an ADR specifying the exact bit-level algorithm (recommended SplitMix64 over FNV-1a accumulator) must be written and approved before rand() in packages/core can be implemented. This blocks IDEA-002 if not resolved first.

Rounding mode enforcement mechanism is a DEFINIR item: an ADR must specify how calling division without an explicit mode is made a compile error or blocking lint error before arithmetic helpers in packages/core are implemented.

FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires a minimum Electron installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI. This is not a deferred concern — the spec states the installer must exist in FASE-1 even if the application does little, to surface ABI and packaging issues early. Electron scaffolding in apps/desktop must be included in FASE-1 scope.
